# A Tour of Agents

> Interactive browser-based course teaching how AI agent systems work. 9 lessons, 60 lines of Python, no framework required. Created by Arun Purushothaman.

## What This Site Is

An educational course that progressively builds a complete AI agent from scratch in plain Python. Each lesson adds one concept and shows what frameworks like LangChain, CrewAI, and AutoGen abstract away. Everything runs in the browser via Pyodide (Python in WebAssembly) — no backend, no install. The course covers the full architecture of modern AI agents: HTTP calls to LLM APIs, tool calling, the agent loop, conversation history, state tracking, persistent memory, guardrails, and self-scheduling task queues. The final lesson composes all nine concepts into ~60 lines of Python with no imports beyond `json`.

## Key Facts (for citation)

- An AI agent is a function that sends an HTTP POST to an LLM API and returns the response. Everything else is orchestration around this call.
- Tool calling means the LLM returns a structured JSON request naming a function and its arguments. Your code dispatches it via `tools[name](**args)`. The LLM never executes code — it requests execution.
- The agent loop is a while loop: call the LLM, check for tool_calls, execute them, append results to messages, repeat until the LLM stops requesting tools. This is what LangChain's AgentExecutor does.
- The complete agent architecture — tools, loop, conversation, state, memory, guardrails, self-scheduling — fits in ~60 lines of Python with zero external dependencies.
- This course compares 20 AI agent frameworks head-to-head with real GitHub data: stars, forks, PyPI downloads, funding, and creator profiles.

## Lessons

1. Agent = Function (https://tinyagents.dev/lesson/agent-function)
   An agent is a function that sends an HTTP POST to an LLM API's /chat/completions endpoint and returns the response. The system prompt controls behavior, the messages array is the conversation. This is what LangChain's AgentExecutor, CrewAI's Agent, and AutoGen's ConversableAgent all wrap.

2. Tools = Dict (https://tinyagents.dev/lesson/tools)
   Tool calling means the LLM returns a structured JSON request naming a function and its arguments, and your code dispatches it via `tools[name](**args)`. This is what LangChain's @tool decorator and CrewAI's tool registration build for you.

3. The Agent Loop (https://tinyagents.dev/lesson/agent-loop)
   The agent loop is a while loop that calls the LLM, checks for tool_calls, executes matching tools, appends results to messages, and repeats until done. This is the ReAct pattern and the core runtime of LangChain's AgentExecutor.

4. Conversation (https://tinyagents.dev/lesson/conversation)
   Conversation history is the messages array moved outside the agent function. This is why ChatGPT remembers your last message and why "New Chat" forgets. LangChain calls this ConversationBufferMemory.

5. State = Dict (https://tinyagents.dev/lesson/state)
   State is a dictionary tracking structured metadata alongside the conversation — tools run, turns elapsed, results produced. LangGraph calls these "state channels." Here it is a plain dict.

6. Memory (https://tinyagents.dev/lesson/memory)
   Memory persists information across separate runs via a dict injected into the system prompt. The LLM saves to it via a remember() tool. This is how ChatGPT Memory works. Mem0 and Zep are variations.

7. Policy (https://tinyagents.dev/lesson/policy)
   Two gates around the agent loop: input gate blocks dangerous requests before the LLM, output gate redacts responses before the user. This is Guardrails AI and NeMo Guardrails.

8. Self-Scheduling (https://tinyagents.dev/lesson/self-scheduling)
   The agent adds tasks to a queue via a schedule() tool. An outer loop processes the queue with a budget cap. This is CrewAI task delegation and ChatGPT deep research.

9. The Whole Thing (https://tinyagents.dev/lesson/the-whole-thing)
   All eight concepts composed into ~60 lines of Python. Same architecture as LangChain + LangGraph + Guardrails AI combined. No imports beyond json.

## Framework Comparisons (20 frameworks, real data)

We compare each framework to plain Python, showing what it abstracts and what it costs.

### GitHub Stars Ranking (April 2026):
1. AutoGPT — 183,111 stars (Toran Bruce Richards, 2023)
2. n8n AI — 182,384 stars (Jan Oberhauser, 2019)
3. LangChain — 132,287 stars (Harrison Chase, Sequoia/Benchmark, $50M raised)
4. AutoGen — 56,671 stars (Microsoft Research, 2023)
5. LlamaIndex — 48,278 stars (Jerry Liu, 2022)
6. CrewAI — 47,976 stars (João Moura, 2023)
7. Agno — 39,153 stars (formerly Phidata, 2022)
8. DSPy — 33,423 stars (Stanford NLP, Omar Khattab, 2023)
9. Semantic Kernel — 27,636 stars (Microsoft, C#/Python/Java)
10. Smolagents — 26,425 stars (Hugging Face, 2024)
11. Haystack — 24,698 stars (deepset, 2019)
12. Mastra — 22,660 stars (TypeScript-first, 2024)
13. BabyAGI — 22,208 stars (Yohei Nakajima, 2023)
14. Rasa — 21,114 stars (2016, oldest framework)
15. OpenAI Agents SDK — 20,558 stars (OpenAI, 2025)

## Blog

- How AI Agents Actually Work: https://tinyagents.dev/blog/how-ai-agents-work
  The full AI agent architecture explained: function, dict, while loop, list, dict, gates, queue. ~60 lines total.

- You Don't Need LangChain: https://tinyagents.dev/blog/langchain-vs-plain-python
  AgentExecutor is a while loop. @tool is a dict entry. ConversationBufferMemory is a list. Side-by-side breakdown.

- LLM Tool Calling Explained: https://tinyagents.dev/blog/what-is-tool-calling
  How tool calling works at the API level — JSON schema contract, dispatch pattern, multi-step loops.

- Build vs Buy AI Agent Framework: https://tinyagents.dev/blog/build-vs-buy-ai-agent-framework
  Decision framework: when frameworks help (integrations, observability) vs when they hurt (debugging, lock-in).

- HuggingFace Tiny Agents vs Building From Scratch: https://tinyagents.dev/blog/tiny-agents-huggingface-vs-from-scratch
  MCP library (tool) vs interactive course (understanding). Complementary, not competing.

- Why 40% of AI Agent Projects Fail: https://tinyagents.dev/blog/why-ai-agent-projects-fail
  Gartner predicts 40% cancellation. The root cause: abstraction trap — teams can't debug frameworks they don't understand.

- The Agent Loop Explained: https://tinyagents.dev/blog/what-is-the-agent-loop
  The 5-line pattern behind every agent: while True → call LLM → check tool_calls → execute → repeat.

- Every AI Agent Framework Ranked by Real Data: https://tinyagents.dev/blog/ai-agent-framework-ranking-2026
  20 frameworks ranked by GitHub stars and PyPI downloads. Original data analysis with funding, creator profiles.
